findings.title: Speech fixed as an extending liability
findings.claim: The focus sets the spoken boast down in writing and adds punishment to its speaker. Against the earlier promise of wealth and offspring, the later inheritance of what he says turns the expected inflow around: the claim is carried into a written liability whose extension has a temporal and cumulative edge.

The nearby challenge about unseen knowledge or covenant qualifies the boast; 19:77 names what he expects to receive, while 19:80 reverses the direction through inheritance. The delay-and-count wording in 19:84 and the exhaustive count in 19:94 let the extension be heard against measured accounting.
findings.reader_payoff: The threat becomes more than a note for later: a forecast of acquisition is entered into an account that grows into punishment and is tied to the claimant himself.
findings.containment: The wording does not settle whether what is inherited in 19:80 is the utterance, the possessions it claims, or a metonymic relation between them. The ink image is a bounded resonance of writing meeting the M-D-D branch, not a claim about the physical medium. The count may concern persons or their allotted time; no duration is specified.

epistemic.reason: The channel nomination and its support are trusted, and the supplied words ground the record, punishment, and inheritance relation. The integrated liability and ink images remain interpretive and are kept within the cited pericope.

findings.title: Writing beside the disappearance of voice
findings.claim: The focus says the speaker's words will be written. At the section's end, earlier generations are gone and no one can sense or hear them, not even a faint sound. The juxtaposition lets writing stand as a different kind of trace beside a voice that has vanished.
findings.mechanism: The spoken-word carrier in the focus meets the written-text carrier; 19:98 then places destroyed communities beside denied hearing and the absence of even a faint sound. Their contact makes the focus's record a counterpoint to acoustic disappearance.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can feel the difference between a voice that depends on a living speaker and a written record that has been set down.
findings.containment: The final verse does not say that a record survives the destroyed communities; it says that no one is sensed or heard. Durability beyond the speaker is an inference, and total disappearance remains a live alternative.

epistemic.reason: The HFT trace's focus and closing-context coordinates match the supplied surface and roots. The contrast is grounded, but the persistence of a written record beyond destruction is not stated and remains bounded as inference.

friction_notes: The legacy_unbound HFT records supply exact Arabic anchors and word positions, and the lean context roots align with those coordinates; their branch roles remain attributed nominations rather than independent lexical records.

The pebble and separated-bead images are bounded analogies: the context counts and individuates people but does not name stones, pearls, or a string. The timed-count image also lacks a named duration or unit.

The utterance-to-fracture and record-to-vanished-voice findings remain inferences. Their boundaries preserve the alternatives that the later collapse is rhetorical evaluation and that no written record is asserted to survive destruction.

The automatic host basmala was considered in Phase 1; the external overlay 1:2–1:7 was considered only in Phase 2. Neither adds a focus-linked semantic delta beyond the native pericope's covenant, count, punishment, and solitary-return context.
